description: Xenon is a chemical element with symbol Xe and atomic number 54. It is a dense, colorless, odorless noble gas found in Earth's atmosphere in trace amounts. Although generally unreactive, it can undergo chemical reactions such as the formation of xenon hexafluoroplatinate, the first noble gas compound to be synthesized.
uses: Xenon is used in flash lamps and arc lamps, and as a general anesthetic. It is used in excimer laser designs and as a pump in laser designs. Xenon is also used to search for hypothetical weakly interacting massive particles and as a propellant for ion thrusters in spacecraft.
characteristics: Xenon has a density of 5.894 kg/m³ at standard temperature and pressure, about 4.5 times the density of Earth's atmosphere. As a liquid, it has high polarizability and is an excellent solvent capable of dissolving hydrocarbons, biological molecules, and water. Under gigapascals of pressure, xenon forms a metallic phase that appears sky blue, and when excited by electrical discharge in a gas-filled tube, it emits a blue or lavenderish glow.
